Iowa won, 58-48. Jim Slosiarek/The Gazette IOWA CITY — This is March, yes.Felt like August.A warm spell, coupled with the fact that Carver-Hawkeye Arena is not air conditioned, made the 43-year-old arena a stifling place Saturday afternoon.According to a facilities representative, a courtside thermometer recorded the heat peak at 90 degrees during Iowa’s 58-48 win over Fairleigh Dickinson in a first-round NCAA women’s basketball game.“Coming out for warmups, it was like a smack in the face how hot it was in there,” FDU’s Ava Renninger said. “I already sweat a lot as it is. There was a towel or two towels given to me every timeout, every break possible.“It was really hot, but I don't think it affected how we played.”FDU played well enough to make the Hawkeyes — and the crowd of 14,332 — perspire.“We knew it was going to be pretty hot with the weather, and also with a lot of fans there,” said Iowa’s Chit-Chat Wright, who is used to the Southern heat of Atlanta. “We focused on hydrating and making sure that we got the hydration where we needed.”Iowa’s Ava Heiden said, “We practice in that gym in the summer in the full Carver heat, so I think we're used to it for the most part. Iowa women's basketball Ava Heiden after defeating FDU in the first round of the NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament March 21, 2026. Video: Jeff Linder/The Gazette 📱 Follow us: Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/GazetteOnIowa Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/gazetteoniowa X: https://x.com/GazetteOnIowa BlueSky: https://bsky.app/profile/thegazettesports.bsky.social “Just a little early-summer feel for us.”Heiden converted 11 of 16 shots, 7 of 7 free throws in a career-high 29-point performance.The court was probably 10-15 degrees warmer than both the tunnel and the concourse.“The first warmup, I guess, it kind of hit us. It was warm,” FDU’s Madlena Gerke said. “We really felt that like this was going to be a different atmosphere and different weather, you could say.”Iowa (27-6) plays Virginia (21-11) in the second round Monday, with the winner moving on to the Sweet 16 in Sacramento.Monday’s forecasted high is 51.Finally, some non-chalkIt took 20 games, but finally a lower seed prevailed in the first round.Virginia.The 10-seed Cavaliers rallied from a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit and eliminated 7-seed Georgia 82-73 in overtime in Saturday’s opener at Carver.Virginia had been a First Four contestant, outlasted Arizona State 57-55 in the first round, then ruled the extra 5 minutes Saturday.Kymora Johnson scored 28 points, and Sa’Myah Johnson hit 10 of 12 shots in a 23-point outing.Romi Levy banked home a 3-pointer with 1:27 left in regulation to tie it, 71-71.Mia Woolfork led Georgia (22-10) with 27 points, but missed two free throws with 1:03 left in regulation that would have put the Lady Bulldogs ahead.
